thread:
maria: quick check — ACME just sent a data-erase request that mentions traces + request logs. before i open the formal ticket: what's the minimal safe checklist so we don't accidentally remove things we need for debugging / billing?
raj: short answer: confirm request ID + legal ok, identify all payload locations, enforce hold on exports, then run scrub tool. cc @taylor for privacy signoff.
mar ia: yep i'll get the legal id, thanks. where's the scrub tool? last time we used a one-off aws rm which freaked people out.
raj: we have an internal tool: `erase-traces` in infra-tools. usage example:
```
./infra-tools/erase-traces --customer acme-corp --paths traces,requests --since 2022-01-01 --dry-run
```
important: always run `--dry-run` first and check the manifest. the tool writes a manifest to S3: `s3://redwood-erasure-manifests/acme-corp/<ts>.json` and you must attach that to the ticket.
taylor: privacy here — filing checklist:
1) legal signed request id (ticket link)
2) customer identity verification (email match + account owner)
3) retention exceptions check (any holds from compliance)
4) backup & export freeze (kick off hold in backup pipeline)
5) run dry-run + attach manifest
6) approval from data-erasure-approvers group
we require privacy + one approver from security for anything PII.
alex: note: logs live in multiple places — request-logs (kafka -> bigquery), route traces (s3), and ephemeral caches (redis). make sure the tool scopes everything; otherwise we'll leak copies.
maria: thanks. who can approve the final deletion? is that a single person or a group?
raj: approvers: privacy leads (taylor or me if delegated) + security oncall or any member of `data-erasure-approvers` Slack group. if this affects billing or needs customer notification, product must ok (alex).
security-bot: policy snippet: "Permanent deletion must be authorized by Privacy + Security. Manifests stored for audit for 90 days. Do not run `aws s3 rm` directly unless instructed by infra-admin." <https://redwood.internal/policies/data-erasure>
alex: timeline: if you get legal id today and privacy signs off, eng-sre can run dry-run today and schedule deletion tomorrow noon (UTC) to avoid peak. want to do canary on a small prefix first.
raj: agreed. canary example:
```
./infra-tools/erase-traces --customer acme-corp --paths traces --prefix canary-2026-03 --dry-run
```
then inspect manifest and do full run with `--confirm`.
maria: perfect. i'll gather legal id and ping @data-erasure-approvers once i have manifests. will post ticket link here.
security-bot: :lock: reminder: audit logs will be auto-attached to ticket. anyone running the tool must use `infra-eraser` role or the `infra-deleter` profile.
raj: adding one more: double-check third-party sinks (datadog, sentry). those need separate purge steps — contact obs team.
taylor: i'll prepare the privacy approval template for the ticket and CC legal.
maria: thank you all — creating ticket now, will paste updates.
